social exchange relationships at the workplace (e.g., leader-member exchange, team-member exchange, and supervisor-subordinate relationships) moderate the relationship between personality and performance (i.e., task performance, citizenship performance, and counterproductive behavior).
high-quality social exchange relationships weaken the relationships between personality and task performance, and between personality and citizenship performance.
the effects of personality traits on task and citizenship performance depend on the nature of social exchange relationships.

the effects of social exchange in the workplace.

the effects of personality on performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

social exchange theory and trait activation theory can be integrated into a more complete understanding of the effects of social exchange on performance, and that personality traits can moderate the effects of social exchanges.
the joint effects of personality (conscientiously) and workplace social exchange (leader-member exchange) are significant and positive in predicting task performance.
the joint effects of personality traits and social exchange relationships at the work place are important predictors of employee performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of a social exchange relationship at work can weaken the positive relationship between personality traits and employee performance.
the social exchange relationships between leaders and their subordinates and among team members moderate the relationships between personality and work outcomes.
the social environment can influence the relationship between traits and performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the quality of social exchange relationships can be a moderator of the relationship between personality and performance, such that when the quality of the social exchange relationships is high, the effects of personality on performance are weaker.
personality and social exchange relationships interact to predict performance, and this interaction is stronger for performance outcomes than it is for the predictors.
the quality of social exchange relationships can be used as a moderating factor to explain why some employees perform better than others.
